subject: Life Skills
title: The Distraction Audit
description: A quick win: understand The Distraction Audit.

hook.text: He tracked every interruption for one week. Phone: 76 times. Slack: 52 times. Random browsing: 34 times.

buildup.text: Most people think they are interrupted rarely. Data reveals the real picture is far worse than their guess.

discovery.text: An audit is simple: each time you get pulled away, jot a tally mark. Categorize at the end of the day.

twist.text: Half of all distractions are self-inflicted. You opened that app yourself. External interruptions are the minority.

climax.text: Fix the top offender first. One change — like silencing your phone during focus blocks — often cuts distractions in.

punchline.text: Measure the leaks before you plug them.

quiz.question: What do distraction audits usually reveal?
options: About half of distractions are self-inflicted
People are interrupted less often than they think
